The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Republican Challenger in New York Makes Final Push in Key Race for House Control
item.description:
A Republican challenging a vulnerable Democratic incumbent in one of the nation's most competitive House races is touting a key endorsements. Mike LiPetri, a former New York state assembly member is heavily backed by President Donald Trump in his contest against Rep. Tom Suozzi, D-N.Y., who won back the suburban swing seat in 2024 after Rep. George Santos was ousted in scandal. National Republicans view Suozzi as a top target and look to make gains in the district spanning parts of Long Island and Queens in November’s elections.
FOX’s Gurnal Scott speaks with Mike LiPetri, Republican Candidate for Congress in New York's 3rd District, who makes his case that he is right candidate for all New Yorkers.

item.title: Can Republicans Rally Rural Voters to Save Their Majority?
item.description:
With the midterm elections less than two weeks away, President Trump is continuing his crisscross around the country to rally his base across deep red strongholds and battleground states. FOX News contributor and former White House Deputy Chief of Staff Karl Rove joins White House correspondent Aishah Hasnie to examine voter sentiment in the heartland as economic pressures strain rural communities. Plus, Rove weighs in on tightening margins in Florida, and whether there is still room for an October surprise before Election Day.
Following the Supreme Court's decision not to take up the case, debate continues over the ongoing legal delays and procedural hurdles in prosecuting the 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and his co-defendants at Guantanamo Bay. FOX News contributor and George Washington University law professor Jonathan Turley joins to discuss the D.C. Circuit's ruling allowing the Secretary of Defense to set aside 9/11 plea deals, explaining how past torture complicates evidence, why a 2028 trial is achievable, and why the case belonged in civilian court from the start.
PLUS, commentary by Jason Rantz, author of What’s Killing America, and the host of The Jason Rantz Show.

item.title: What is Fueling Destructive French Riots and Could It Happen in The U.S.?
item.description:
What began weeks ago as student-led demonstrations over classroom conditions has escalated into widespread riots involving a range of political and ideological factions across France over the weekend. Over 2,500 people have been arrested and damages have exceeded $1B after the protests spiraled out of control. There seems to be up to 54 organizations, only 16 are student groups, and the others include communist groups, labor unions and political activists in the network promoting the riots and protests in France.
FOX’s Jonathan Savage speaks with Lance Hunter, Professor of International Relations at Augusta University and expert in political violence, who says while the protests may have started with legitimate political concerns, they open the door to criminal elements with a more malicious agenda.

item.title: Iowans Are ‘Frustrated’. Can Ashley Hinson Keep It Red?
item.description:
With control of the Senate on the line, the final two weeks of campaigning are critical for Republicans in Iowa. GOP Senate candidate Ashley Hinson joins the Rundown to make her case to voters. She discusses affordability, rural healthcare, and the challenges facing farmers. Hinson also weighs in on President Trump's upcoming visit to Iowa and his decision to ease sanctions on Russia.
Debates over gun violence in the U.S. often miss the mark due to political gridlock and common misconceptions surrounding the issue. Author and host of the Revisionist History podcast Malcolm Gladwell discusses insights from his book, The American Way of Killing: The Invention of an Epidemic, addressing misunderstandings about assault rifle bans and mass shooting statistics. He argues that high U.S. homicide rates stem primarily from under-policing compared to European nations, how modern medical advancements have reduced firearm fatalities, and traces the Second Amendment's roots to 18th-century slave patrols—advocating for a shift from federal gun control theater toward effective homicide prevention and state-level policy.
PLUS, commentary by David Marcus, columnist for FOX News Digital.

item.title: Key Race That Could Help The GOP Keep Control of the Senate
item.description:
The battle for Texas is reaching a boiling point as early voting begins, with a record 19 million-plus Texans registered to vote. Democrat James Talarico is courting independents and moderate Republicans, while Republican Ken Paxton and national GOP leaders are painting him as a far-left Democrat out of step with Texas voters. With just about two weeks until Election Day, candidates are making their final pushes and bringing out party heavyweights to turn out voters.
FOX’s Jessica Rosenthal speaks with Senator James Lankford (R-OK) who is urging Republican voters to get to the polls and shares his thoughts on some key races like the fierce Senate race in Texas.

item.title: How Control Of Congress Comes Down To Candidate Quality
item.description:
With Election Day approaching, FOX News Radio political analyst Josh Kraushaar joins the Rundown to break down the Senate and House races to watch, the latest fundraising numbers, and how candidate quality could influence the results. While Democrats appear to have the advantage, Kraushaar explains why the size of their potential gains remains uncertain and how voter turnout could determine whether Republicans face a difficult night or a historic Democratic wave. Plus, what could the midterm results signal about the future direction of the Democratic Party heading into 2028?
Breast cancer death rates in the United States have dropped significantly over the past four decades, driven primarily by advancements in early screenings and personalized risk detection. FOX News Contributor and triple board certified physician in emergency medicine, medical toxicology and addiction medicine Dr. Stephanie Widmer joins the Rundown to break down updated mammogram screening guidelines, and how AI is assisting radiology and emerging treatments.
PLUS, commentary by Guy Benson, FOX News political analyst and host of FOX News Radio's The Guy Benson Show.
